subject.title: Feature: browser upload tool fallback for non-standard file inputs (ByteUploader)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit Browser file-injection mode for custom uploaders, and if so should it be DataTransfer drop, clipboard paste, native CDP drag, or a narrower named API?
rationale: This would move local managed files outside the standard file-input boundary into page-controlled handlers, so automation should not choose a silent fallback or security semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add explicit drop-file tool mode
options.body: Create a named Browser upload mode that validates managed paths, targets a caller-specified drop zone, documents security semantics, and proves a ByteUploader-style page live.

options.title: Keep standard upload only
options.body: Leave Browser upload limited to file chooser, direct file input, and Chrome MCP upload_file, and document that custom uploader automation must use site-specific scripts or plugins.

options.title: Prototype behind maintainer-only review
options.body: Allow a guarded experimental API discussion or PR, but do not queue autonomous implementation until the security and live proof requirements are agreed.

recommendation.title: Add explicit drop-file tool mode
recommendation.body: Create a named Browser upload mode that validates managed paths, targets a caller-specified drop zone, documents security semantics, and proves a ByteUploader-style page live.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current history on Browser upload ownership and the adjacent chooser/upload API fix.
